chunks: Termination networks. The question: Describe some termination networks.
A termination network is a few parts, usually resistors, sometimes with a capacitor or diode, that stop a signal from bouncing back along a line.
Common ones are series, parallel, Thevenin (split), AC, diode clamp and differential. They differ in wasted power, how much they shrink the signal, and where they must sit.
Think of ways to tame a ball rolling down a hallway. A soft mat at the start (series) lets one bounce come back and die there.
A catcher at the far end (parallel) stops it for good, but works all day. A catcher who only reaches out when the ball moves (AC) rests in between.
Rails along the sides (diode clamp) only keep it from flying out.
Here is the key diagram for this question.
Series termination: a resistor at the driver so R out plus R s equals Z 0 ("Series vs parallel termination tradeoffs").
Parallel termination: a resistor equal to Z 0 from the line end to ground or a fixed voltage ("Source vs sink termination and matching").
Thevenin (split) termination: one resistor to the supply and one to ground. Together they act like Z 0 and set a resting voltage.
AC termination: Z 0 in series with a capacitor, so no steady (DC) current flows. Differential termination: one resistor across a pair, such as 100 ohms.
Take a 3. 3 volts driver with 20 ohms output impedance on a 50 ohms line. A 30 ohms series resistor wastes no steady power.
A 50 ohms resistor to ground leaves the receiver only 3. 3 times 50 over 70 equals 2. 36 volts as its high level, and the driver supplies 3. 3 over 70 about 47 milliamps.
A Thevenin pair of 100 ohms and 100 ohms acts like 50 ohms, rests the line at 1. 65 volts, and burns a steady 54 milliwatts. That is the whole idea.

"The common termination networks are: series, a resistor at the source so R out plus R s equals Z 0 , no DC power; parallel, Z 0 from the end of the line to ground or V TT , which costs DC power; Thevenin, two resistors to the rails with parallel value Z 0 , which also sets a bias; AC, Z 0 in series with a capacitor, no DC current; diode clamps for overshoot; and a differential resistor across a pair, often on-die.
I pick by topology and power: series for point-to-point, parallel or Thevenin for multi-drop, differential for pairs."
